title: South East Queensland Water Security Program
notes: Covers SEQ Water Grid operations, Wyaralong connection planning, Gold Coast desalination expansion business case and Western Corridor recycled-water use.

title: Recycled Water
notes: Western Corridor Recycled Water Scheme retained as drought-response and longer-term supply option.

title: Water storage / Greater Sydney system
notes: Greater Sydney uses 11 major supply dams linked by rivers, pipes and canals; Warragamba capacity 2,064,680 ML and supplies roughly 80% of Sydney drinking water via Prospect WFP.

title: ACT-QBN water storage levels
notes: Total usable dam storage around 278 GL after enlarged Cotter; Murrumbidgee-to-Googong transfer supplements storage.

title: Googong Dam
notes: 119.4 GL storage on Queanbeyan River; major ACT/QBN source.

title: Melbourne Water Outlook 2026
notes: Tracks storage, inflow, demand and desalination response; 2026 dry conditions triggered 150 GL desalination order.

title: Water Security Plan for Melbourne Geelong and connected towns
notes: South-Central Water Grid serves over 80% of Victoria; government says up to an additional 95 GL/year may be needed by 2030 beyond existing desalination capacity.

title: Victorian desalination
notes: Wonthaggi plant up to 150 GL/year; 84 km two-way transfer pipeline into south-central grid.

title: Riverina Water supply system
notes: Wagga system combines Murrumbidgee River and multiple groundwater borefields; regulated river flows influenced by Burrinjuck and Blowering dams.

title: Wagga Wagga Water Treatment Plant
notes: 55 ML/day treatment plant opened 2021; supports broader Riverina Water network and growth to 2050.

title: Albury water cycle
notes: Murray River below Hume is source; two plants each up to 70 ML/day plus separate raw-water industrial network.

title: Goulburn water supply services
notes: Pejar 9,000 ML, Sooley 6,250 ML and Rossi Weir 330 ML are principal listed storages.

title: Where our water comes from
notes: Cressbrook 81,842 ML, Cooby 21,166 ML, Perseverance 30,140 ML; 47 bore stations provide about 20-30%; Wivenhoe pipeline is 38 km and can transfer 14.2 GL/year with 18 GL/year ultimate capacity.

title: Water Vision 2071
notes: Long-horizon plan: treatment/pumping/allocation upgrades, four-community connection and new/major source infrastructure required from the mid-2040s.

title: 2026-27 Annual Budget water capital
notes: $81.4m Cressbrook Dam Safety Improvement in 2026-27 plus Perseverance raw main capacity renewal, Cooby inlet works, Greenmount/Four Communities and Highfields reservoir works.

title: Toowoomba to Warwick Pipeline
notes: Approx 111 km project with >$300m funding; staged March 2026, using Wivenhoe water through existing Toowoomba infrastructure; Stage 1 reaches Greenmount and four growing communities.

title: Lower Hunter Water Security Plan
notes: Diversified strategy includes conservation, recycling, desalination and potential Upper Hunter inter-regional connection; explicitly plans for climate/growth uncertainty.

title: Belmont Desalination Plant
notes: Permanent plant under construction; up to 30 ML/day rainfall-independent supply, about 15% of average daily regional demand; major marine works completed August 2026.

title: Tamworth 2026 water security evidence
notes: Current program includes new Dungowan Pipeline connection, Calala raw-water storage, Manilla pumping upgrade and smart metering; 2026 source confirms primary Chaffey plus Dungowan operating strategy.

title: Tamworth water entitlements and drought context
notes: Tamworth entitlements listed as 16.4 GL/year Peel/Chaffey, 5.6 GL/year Dungowan and 1.055 GL/year groundwater; source notes two severe droughts in 20 years and near-runout risk.

title: Water usage and supply
notes: Malpas main storage about 13 GL with stated expansion capability to 26 GL; Puddledock emergency storage; Guyra dams and groundwater program.

title: Regional Water Security Project
notes: Stage 1 restores Oaky River Dam, builds 54 km transfer to Armidale WTP and extends supply to Uralla; Stage 2 raises Malpas after demand growth. Dry-year Armidale requirement stated as 4,480 ML/year.

title: Armidale Water Security Project
notes: State Significant Infrastructure process formally underway; current portal status More Information Required.

title: Regional water security and NEREZ demand
notes: Council estimates full water-security package spare capacity about 4 GL/year, while peak NEREZ construction demand for Armidale-Uralla-Walcha could exceed four times that spare capacity; useful constraint signal, not a permanent-demand forecast.
